decisions.executionNote: Begin symmetric elbow-up approach, raising clearance slightly and pitching grippers toward the tools; table height and fingertip offset still uncertain.
Retry from unchanged origin with smaller translation and pitch increments to satisfy joint continuity.
Continue pitching downward above the outer hammer and pliers, advancing gradually with open grippers.
Finish near-vertical grasp orientation and approach slowly, using wrist views to refine hammer and plier alignment before descent.
Correct lateral alignment from wrist views; retain observed height rather than pushing through the descent residual. Approach hammer shaft and narrower plier section.
Fine-center the hammer shaft and plier neck in the jaws, then close both grippers at the observed tabletop grasp height.
Lift both closed grasps vertically to check actual retention in RGB before transporting to the matching recesses.
Both tools visibly lifted. Transport inward with clearance and small yaw corrections toward their longitudinal toolbox recesses; keep arms on their own sides.
Move above the central hammer and right-side plier recesses at transport height; inspect slot alignment before lowering or opening.
Replan smaller inward-and-downward increments after IK rejection. Seat retained hammer over its recess; right pliers appear slipped, so move right arm outward for recovery.
Release the hammer onto its recess and lift clear to inspect seating. Open the right jaws and approach the slipped pliers more proximally for a stable regrasp.
Withdraw left outward while lifting to avoid the high inward reach limit. Right approaches the plier pivot rather than the splayed handles.
Left approaches the wrench with yaw restored. Right narrows around the exposed metal section of the slipped pliers and closes for recovery; retention uncertain.
Center and lower onto the wrench handle. Right releases the obstructed grasp and lifts outward, changing jaw direction to approach the tape measure without straddling the tray wall.
Close and test-lift the centered wrench. Lower the right open gripper over the tape with jaws oriented fore-aft to clear the toolbox edge.
Transport the visibly retained wrench above the left narrow recess. Fine-center the tape from its wrist image, lower slightly and close the right jaws.
Lower the wrench toward the narrow left interior slot with small continuity-preserving increments. Test-lift the tape measure before inward transport.
Wrench appears displaced by the tray edge, so withdraw the left jaws for recovery. Move the retained tape over the rounded front-right recess with clearance.
Tape slipped at the rim; recover with a deeper grasp and separate high horizontal transport from descent. Reorient left jaws fore-aft to avoid the wall when recovering the wrench.
Approach the wrench near its exposed head and lower the right gripper vertically around the displaced tape; keep both jaws open for visual centering.
Make small wrist-based centering corrections and close at a deeper grasp height, then begin a short vertical retention test.
Raise the tape fully above the toolbox rim before transporting. Recenter the left jaws onto the wrench neck rather than the empty space beside it and test a short lift.
Keep tape high during inward transport to the rounded recess; do not descend across the rim. Lift the wrench vertically to establish whether its jaw contact retains it.
Both recovery grasps slipped. Reapproach the now-exposed wrench handle and tape from above with lateral jaws, avoiding the tray and using slower, centered grasps.
Retry the unchanged poses using smaller backward and yaw increments, lowering slightly to stay away from the inward high-reach continuity limit.
Finish lateral-jaw alignment and descend over the wrench handle and tape at their updated positions, keeping open until close-up alignment is confirmed.
Close on the centered wrench handle and lift. The pliers obstruct the tape, so move right to the plier pivot with reduced jaw opening to clear the nearby tray wall.
Move left grasp to the protruding wrench handle beyond the front rim and correct verticality. Right descends around the narrower plier pivot using a smaller aperture to avoid the wall.
Fine-center on the protruding wrench tip and plier metal pivot, descend to deeper side contact, then close without lateral motion.
Lift the deeper centered grasps vertically with both jaws closed; verify retention before any horizontal motion.
Wrench was not retained. Move left toward the misplaced hammer for correction. Raise and pitch the retained pliers to reduce dangling depth before crossing the tray rim.
Replan away from the rejected pitch. Bring left jaws toward the hammer shaft for in-tray correction while right retracts outward and restores its downward approach orientation.
Retry with halved right-arm increments after zero-step rejection; left still approaches the hammer without crossing center.
Use smaller inward steps for the hammer head region. The pliers now lie flatter; align right jaws across their metal pivot rather than grasping their thin edge.
Avoid the left inward IK limit by moving link6 outward and tilting the fingers inward. Lower right around the visually centered flat plier pivot and close.
Reduce left translation and inward tilt further after the zero-step continuity rejection. Right retains the planned centered plier descent and closure.
Tilt the left fingertips inward toward the hammer while preserving elbow-up reach margin. Test-lift the right grasp and inspect whether the pliers are retained independently of the tape.
Lower the tilted left grasp around the hammer handle. Transport the visibly retained pliers slowly at clearance height while rotating their head toward the back of the matching recess.
Close on the hammer and lift outward for reach margin. Continue slow, level plier transport and complete its lengthwise alignment above the right recess.
Refine both tools' lengthwise alignment while retained. Center pliers over their recess before final vertical descent; correct the hammer's diagonal orientation with a small yaw.
Separate the wrists before seating tools. Hold the hammer stationary while moving the retained pliers outward and correcting their observed diagonal orientation.
Seat the now-straight hammer into its central recess with a small rightward and downward motion; keep the pliers stationary away from the left wrist.
Release the aligned hammer and withdraw outward to expose its seating. Begin small plier alignment and descent only as the left wrist clears.
Lower and advance the retained pliers into the right longitudinal recess. Withdraw and straighten the left wrist for wrench recovery without disturbing the released hammer.
Shift pliers slightly right and straighten their observed diagonal before release into the recess. Approach the exposed wrench handle with reduced aperture to clear the toolbox edge.
Withdraw right from the released pliers to inspect placement. Bring the left jaws lower and farther onto the exposed wrench handle, then close and hold before lifting.
Two tools are visibly released in the tray. Move the wrench grasp clear of the front rim and correct verticality; reset right jaw orientation above the remaining tape measure.
Close the low, centered wrench grasp and test a slow lift. Approach the isolated tape with side-facing jaws; refine centering before closing.
Raise the now-retained wrench above the rim. Advance and center the tape within the right fingers, correcting the remaining pitch error and lowering for a deeper side grasp.
Transport the retained wrench slowly above the left recess without descending over the rim. Close the newly centered tape grasp and make a short vertical retention lift.
Wrench slipped but is now clear of the box; approach its middle with jaws across its new diagonal. Lift the tape vertically to full rim clearance before any lateral transport.
Reduce the wrench aperture to avoid the tray, descend onto its mid-handle and close. Carry the retained tape slowly inward at constant clearance height.
Keep the tape level and centered above its rounded recess. Move the left grasp farther in front of the box to avoid the rim contact that prevented reaching the wrench.
Lower the tape into its rounded front-right position with a small centering correction. Advance the left jaws farther onto the exposed wrench handle and close at tabletop height.
Release the tape in its rounded recess and withdraw right to inspect. Allow the low wrench grasp to settle closed before a short vertical retention test.
Lift the settled wrench grasp vertically above the rim. The other three tools are released in the tray; withdraw the right arm toward its origin without disturbing them.
Advance the securely retained wrench slowly at full clearance and straighten its long axis. Continue the right arm's configuration-continuous return toward origin.
The end-grasp slipped during rotation. Regrasp the wrench nearer its middle, now completely clear of the rim, with jaws matched to its diagonal. Finish the right origin approach.
Fine-center and lower onto the wrench's mid-handle, then hold closed to settle the grasp. Make the final small right-arm origin correction.
Lift the fully settled mid-handle wrench grasp vertically, avoiding yaw or lateral acceleration until retention is confirmed. Keep right at origin.
Advance the retained wrench with slow translation only, separating transport from yaw correction to reduce slipping. Right remains at origin.
Correct wrench yaw slowly in place, keeping translation stopped and the jaws closed; inspect retention before further approach.
Continue the isolated slow yaw correction; the wrench remains visibly between the fingers. Keep both positions fixed and right at origin.
The wrench is now lengthwise and retained. Advance slowly at constant height to the left interior recess; defer descent until the rim is cleared.
The wrench has rolled in the grasp near the rim. Add vertical clearance with a small outward retreat before advancing further; retain closed jaws and inspect the tool.
Recover the slipped wrench by its thicker metal head rather than the thin handle. Approach from the front with a slight forward tilt to avoid the toolbox rim; right stays at origin.
Center the wider metal wrench head in the left jaws, lower cautiously outside the front rim and close. Keep the right arm at origin.
